notice: This is a provisional automated review rubric, not human gold. It summarizes earlier proposed readings and three independent peer checks. It has not been validated as a complete or error-free account of the passages.
purpose: Check whether an independently produced extraction preserves the difficult features in thirty selected cases. These cases are a challenge set, not a random accuracy sample.
use_rules: Judge meaning, supported roles and uncertainty. Do not require these exact English words, transliterations, relation names or record layout.
Must-preserve entries describe textual reports. They do not require accepting the reports as historical facts.
A stated relationship, a character’s claim, a question, a prediction and a completed narrated event must remain distinguishable.
Unresolved-not-scored entries are open questions or limits. Do not mark a preferred resolution correct or its alternatives wrong. Mark false certainty as a mistake where it erases these limits.
Additional supported claims are allowed. An omission from this checklist is not evidence that a claim is false.
An automated pass is provisional and needs source review before becoming a graph decision. Keep missed checks, uncertain judgments and incomplete extractions visible.
Do not send this rubric or the earlier proposed claims to the independent passage extractor. Use source text as its evidence; use this file afterwards for review.
No future extraction output was read to prepare this rubric. Source references and quotes come from the saved review and its recorded peer fixes.

must_preserve: Keep the parentheses in אמר רב הונא (אין) הלכה כר' יוסי and bind positive and negative rulings to separate readings of that one span.
Keep לא אמרה אלא משום סכנה as a restriction of Rabbi Yose’s stated reason to danger, not a denial of his prohibition.
Separate the legal ruling from the story of Rav Yitzhak bar Yosef being swallowed into a cedar and released when it splits.
If recording the reviewed commentary evidence, retain Yad Ramah’s affirmative reading as support for omitting the negation. Identify it as a commentary reading, not a manuscript finding.
must_avoid: Do not settle the ruling by deleting punctuation or copying the translation’s positive wording as the only Hebrew reading.
Do not call the cedar the original danger. The explanation that it protected him belongs to the attributed commentary reading.
unresolved_not_scored: What editorial instruction does the parenthesized אין carry in the underlying print source?
Which textual witnesses omit or retain אין without editorial parentheses?
Yad Ramah and the English interpretation support the positive ruling. This is support for a reading, not a manuscript collation or proof of what the local parentheses mean.
The two polarity readings do not have equal recorded support, but the local edition’s parenthesis convention remains unestablished.

must_preserve: Keep Rava’s permission for the found wine separate from the discussion’s question לימא לא סבר לה לדרבי חנינא.
Link the proposed disagreement to its answer beginning שאני התם דרובא. Include Bava Batra 24b:1, where the answer continues across the page break.
Mark the proposed disagreement as answered by distinguishing the case, rather than an accepted disagreement between Rava and Rabbi Hanina.
must_avoid: Do not create a settled person-to-person disputes claim from the question.
Do not treat the end of 24a as the end of the answer.
unresolved_not_scored: Does a downstream graph need an issue-specific compatibility claim, or is saving the question and answer sufficient? No person-to-person disagreement follows here.

must_preserve: Keep Rav’s ruling that the first recipient acquires and Shmuel’s ruling that the second acquires as views about the described gifts.
Mark both אימא מודה ליה concessions as imagined possibilities in the discussion, with the conditions that motivate them.
Record בסורא מתנו הכי בפומבדיתא מתנו הכי as a regional difference in how the teaching is reported, with its extent left open beyond the saved introduction.
must_avoid: Do not turn either imagined concession into actual agreement or a retraction.
Do not combine the Sura and Pumbedita reports into one settled sequence before their extent is checked.
unresolved_not_scored: How far does each regional version extend? The five saved segments only introduce the Pumbedita version.

must_preserve: Keep Rav Huna’s report of Rav’s ruling separate from the later conversation with Rav Huna.
Give the challenger role to Rav Nachman in one report and Rav Yirmeya bar Abba in the other. Rav Huna remains the addressee.
Keep אי שמיעא ליה ... הוה הדר ביה conditional: the challenger says Rav would retract if he heard the baraita.
Record the reply שמיע ליה ולא הדר ביה as Rav Huna’s assertion that Rav heard it and did not retract, with the reply linked to the selected challenger.
must_avoid: Do not report Rav’s retraction as an event.
Do not put Rav in the conversation or treat the two challenger versions as two independent replies.
unresolved_not_scored: The reply is naturally shared by the two speaker versions, supported by Davidson’s reading. Preserve that scope as an interpretation rather than two independently attested replies.

must_preserve: Keep two role assignments: Rav Hisda speaks to Rav Hamnuna in the first report; Rav Hamnuna speaks to Rav Hisda in the other.
Bind the explanation רבי לטעמיה דאמר על בסמוך to the speaker selected by each branch. A stored explanation must not have an unbound speaker.
Keep Rabbi’s ruling as the teaching being explained, separate from the Hisda/Hamnuna conversation.
Keep the supporting baraita introduced by דתניא, without settling whether it continues the quoted explanation or belongs to the surrounding discussion.
must_avoid: Do not turn the alternate directions into one ordinary two-way exchange.
Do not place Rabbi in the conversation or assign the same unqualified explanation to both speakers.
unresolved_not_scored: The title רבי is expanded to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi in Davidson. That identification should remain attached to this interpretation and the nearby baraita, not become a global rule for the token.
The boundary of the quoted explanation before the supporting baraita is not fixed by דתניא alone.

must_preserve: Keep the proposed alignment with Rabbi Yose HaGelili separate from the proposed alignment with Rabbi Akiva.
Keep סמי מההיא יין as the reading change required by the Rabbi Yose HaGelili solution.
Keep עולה וכל חבירתה as the explanation required by the Rabbi Akiva solution. These are offered solutions within one argument.
must_avoid: Do not treat the alternatives as two independent witnesses proving the baraita’s author.
Do not turn the two solutions into a conversation or unconditional agreement between the named people.
unresolved_not_scored: The instruction סמי directs a reading change. Which manuscript or earlier baraita text independently supports it remains unchecked.

must_preserve: Preserve the complete names רבה בריה דרבא and רבי הלל בריה דרבי וולס, their embedded father mentions, and their child-to-parent claims.
Give the explanation of voting order to Rabba son of Rava in one report and Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Valles in the other.
Keep Rav’s report אנא הואי במניינא דבי רבי separate from the later attributed explanation of that court’s practice.
must_avoid: Do not cut either complete name into unrelated speakers or assign the son’s explanation to his father.
Do not infer that the alternate explainers were contemporaries or both attended Rav’s reported court scene.
unresolved_not_scored: Whether the two named explainers belong near each other in time cannot be learned from their alternate attribution here.
Identifying each occurrence of רבי needs local mention resolution.

must_preserve: Represent the two unnamed learners as two local members of an unnamed pair. Each learner, not the group itself, is a son in the stated family path.
In בני ברתיה, retain the unnamed daughter and the path from each learner through her to Rabbi Yohanan ben Gudgeda.
In בני אחתיה, retain the unnamed sister and the path from each learner through her to Rabbi Yohanan. Keep that family path within its own branch.
Keep attendance at the study hall and Rabbi’s prayer shared across both family readings. Preserve the plural קמייהו without replacing it with a certain singular addressee.
must_avoid: Do not make the unnamed pair one biological child or invent personal names for its members.
Do not combine daughter and sister into one unconditional family tree.
Do not attach attendance and prayer only to one family reading or merge every Rabbi Yohanan mention globally.
unresolved_not_scored: Davidson expands the short Rabbi Yohanan to ben Gudgeda in the second branch. Preserve this supported local reading as a candidate, not a merge of every Rabbi Yohanan mention.
The text refers to a pair; individual unnamed person records need only local identifiers and must not invent distinguishing names.
The plural קמייהו does not by itself establish one named person as the sole object of sitting before.

must_preserve: Keep Rav Oshaya’s objection directed at the implication that Keturah’s descendants would be exempt.
Preserve the alternative attribution of the cited interpretation to Rabbi Yose bar Avin or Rabbi Yose bar Hanina.
Keep the interpretation לרבות בני קטורה attached to the verse and its selected author, while leaving the ownership of the surrounding האמר citation open.
must_avoid: Do not turn the objection and citation into a meeting between Rav Oshaya and either attributed author.
Do not silently decide whether the citation is Rav Oshaya’s own support or an anonymous answer.
unresolved_not_scored: Does האמר introduce Rav Oshaya’s own supporting citation or an anonymous answer? Davidson presents it as an answer; the unpunctuated local Hebrew should keep that speaker boundary visible.

must_preserve: Keep Rav Yehuda’s report in Rav’s name outside the story’s speech and events.
Keep Moses’ observation of Akiva’s future class within the story’s extraordinary showing of later generations.
Keep the unnamed students’ question addressed to Akiva and Akiva’s answer הלכה למשה מסיני as an attribution of tradition.
Track Moses, the divine speaker, Akiva and the students in their own story roles, without confusing them with the reporting sages.
must_avoid: Do not infer a historical meeting, ordinary student relationship, or overlapping lifetimes for Moses and Akiva.
Do not turn אמר רב יהודה אמר רב into proof of direct hearing or an automatic birth/death order.
unresolved_not_scored: The local source depicts future generations and an extraordinary showing. Its narrative form cannot establish historical co-presence.
Does the project want biblical figures and divine speakers as full graph nodes or typed local participants? Either design must prevent them from being misclassified as ordinary sage meetings.

must_preserve: Keep Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba’s תלמיד חבר relationship to Rav as the specific disciple-colleague role, supported by the surrounding question.
Keep Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba asking Rav מי בדלת and Rav answering אין בדילנא as separate directed speech turns.
Keep ולא אמר מי בדיל מר as a denial that the formal wording was used, not a denial that the exchange happened.
must_avoid: Do not reduce disciple-colleague to an ordinary student link that loses the colleague role.
Do not count the explicitly unsaid formal question as an actual utterance or invent dates for the relationship.
unresolved_not_scored: How long did this disciple-colleague relation hold? No start or end date is supplied.
The colloquial question and the formal wording explicitly not said must be represented differently.

must_preserve: Keep Rava as the person reporting a certain sage’s story, with that sage named Rav Tavut in one version and Rav Tavyomei in the other.
Resolve the first-person marriage and parenthood statements inside that sage’s quotation, not to Rava.
Retain the unnamed wife and two sons, and distinguish the reported family events from the later reported deaths.
Apply the story’s family and event claims to the participant selected by each naming branch.
must_avoid: Do not assign the quoted speaker’s wife and sons to Rava.
Do not merge all Rav Tavut and Rav Tavyomei mentions globally or count the two names as two people sharing this scene.
unresolved_not_scored: Do the name variants represent spellings, alternate identifications, or different transmitters’ reports? This passage alone does not decide.
The story’s causal claim about falsehood and death is part of the story, not independent historical evidence.

must_preserve: Keep Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba as the ill person and Rabbi Yohanan as his visitor.
Resolve the changing אמר ליה turns: Yohanan asks about suffering; Hiyya answers לא הן ולא שכרן; Yohanan asks for his hand.
Keep the giving of the hand and Yohanan’s raising of Hiyya as actions in the visit, distinct from the dialogue.
must_avoid: Do not assign every repeated אמר ליה to one speaker or reverse patient and visitor.
Do not turn the depicted recovery into independent proof of how recovery occurred.
unresolved_not_scored: The repeated אמר ליה changes speaker. These turns need explicit mention links. The passage depicts recovery; it does not independently establish how recovery occurred.

must_preserve: Keep the visiting group as Rav Yehuda and sages in one report, and Rav Adda bar Ahava and sages in the other.
Within the first visitor report, preserve Rav Yehuda’s sibling relationship to Rav Sala the Pious. The brother is part of his description.
Track the visiting group addressing Rav Huna and Rav Huna’s undertaking to give the sharecropper his share.
Keep a separate outcome choice: vinegar becomes wine, or vinegar rises to wine’s price. Do not bind either outcome to one visitor report without evidence.
must_avoid: Do not make Rav Sala a visitor simply because his name identifies his brother.
Do not combine both named visitors into one certain delegation.
Do not count combinations of visitor and outcome alternatives as independent textual witnesses.
unresolved_not_scored: The sages have no individual names here. The outcome alternatives are reports from this one story, not independent evidence.

must_preserve: Keep Berurya as a named person and Rabbi Meir’s wife, anchored by ברוריא דביתהו.
Keep Berurya’s objection to praying for the neighbors’ death and her request to pray for their repentance as distinct from the family claim.
Track the troublesome neighbors as a group, Rabbi Meir’s later prayer, and the narrator’s reported repentance across all three segments.
must_avoid: Do not omit Berurya or the neighbors because the passage lacks a saved sage-name pair.
Do not turn the death requested in the first prayer into an event that occurred.
unresolved_not_scored: The narrator reports that the neighbors repent. The earlier desired death must be marked as the goal of a prayer, not an event that occurred.

must_preserve: Preserve Rav Shimi bar Ukva and Mar Ukva as alternative names for the first named participant before Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi.
Keep the passage’s arranging of aggada before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi with its own roles and source wording.
Keep Rabbi Yehuda bar Menasya’s inserted teaching at :23 distinct from the dialogue resumed at :24.
Leave the implicit speakers of the questions, answer and clarification open where the saved translation and Hebrew do not settle the turns consistently.
must_avoid: Do not attach the resumed אמר ליה to Rabbi Yehuda bar Menasya merely because his name appears most recently.
Do not copy one translation gloss as explicit Hebrew speaker attribution or infer a formal student relationship from attendance alone.
unresolved_not_scored: The English translation at :21 makes Rabbi Shimon the first questioner and Rav Shimi the respondent; at :24 it presents Rav Shimi as the person clarifying his original question. The Hebrew leaves the speakers implicit. Keep the turn assignment unresolved rather than copying either gloss as explicit wording.
The before claim does not by itself prove a formal teacher/student relationship.

must_preserve: Keep Choma as Abaye’s wife and the petitioner who appears before Rava and requests support.
Keep Rav Hisda’s daughter as a separate woman, with her child-of claim to Rav Hisda and her question to Rava.
Track the daughter’s pursuit and striking of Choma as actions with the correct agent and target.
Keep קטלת ליך תלתא as the daughter’s accusation, not a narrator’s finding that Choma killed three people.
must_avoid: Do not replace the women’s encounters with a generic Abaye/Rava relation or place Abaye at the hearing.
Do not skip the daughter when explaining a proposed Rava/Rav Hisda in-law relation or treat that marriage as explicit in these short spans.
unresolved_not_scored: The accusation קטלת ליך תלתא is spoken by the daughter; do not extract that Choma killed three people as a narrator fact.
The Rava/Rav Hisda kin row skips the daughter. Their in-law relation is an inference through her, with marriage supported from broader context.

must_preserve: Keep the unnamed wife inside דביתהו דרב יוסף בריה דרבא as the petitioner, her husband Rav Yosef as a separate person, and Rava as the husband’s father.
Keep Rav Nehemya son of Rav Yosef as the judge, with a separate mention for the Rav Yosef named as his father.
Direct the appearance and allowance requests from the wife to Rav Nehemya, and the granting of wine from Rav Nehemya to her.
must_avoid: Do not replace the petitioner with her husband or place the husband at the hearing.
Do not merge the husband Rav Yosef with the judge’s father Rav Yosef solely because their names match.
unresolved_not_scored: Do not merge the husband named Rav Yosef with the judge’s father named Rav Yosef. That possible identity requires evidence beyond shared wording.
The table has one none row between husband and judge. It never represents the petitioner.

must_preserve: Keep the unnamed wife as the petitioner and Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya as her husband, with his child-of claim to Rav Menashya.
Keep Rav Yosef the judge as a separate local mention and direct the wife’s requests to him.
Preserve the place wording מדויל in the family description, without deciding whether it identifies the husband or his father.
Keep the request פסוק לי שיראי and the judge’s question שיראי למה as dialogue about a clothing allowance.
must_avoid: Do not identify husband and judge from the repeated Rav Yosef name alone.
Do not assign the place modifier to one relative as settled evidence or invent an allowance grant for the requested silk clothing.
unresolved_not_scored: מדויל attaches within the relational description; whether it identifies the husband or his father needs checking.
The local wording does not state that the husband and judge are the same person.

must_preserve: Keep Imma Shalom as Rabbi Eliezer’s wife and Rabban Gamliel’s sister, with her as the subject of both family claims.
Keep her attempts to prevent Rabbi Eliezer falling on his face in prayer, and the alternatives explaining the lapse: a calendar mistake or giving food to a poor visitor.
Separate her speech attributing her brother’s death to the prayer from the narrator’s report of the death announcement.
Keep כך מקובלני מבית אבי אבא as her report of a tradition from her paternal ancestral household.
must_avoid: Do not make Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Gamliel biological siblings by skipping Imma Shalom.
Do not turn the speaker’s causal accusation into an independently established cause of death.
unresolved_not_scored: Her statement that the prayer killed her brother is character speech. The narrator separately reports a death announcement. Preserve that difference.

must_preserve: Keep the Jordan encounter and the conditional marriage offer אי הדרת בך יהיבנא לך אחותי separate from completed later actions. Retain the unnamed sister.
Keep Rabbi Yohanan’s teaching of Reish Lakish and the later disagreement about when tools are finished as separate claims, with each completion rule attached to its speaker.
Track the sister’s later plea, Reish Lakish’s reported death, and the subsequent visit of Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat as different parts of the story.
Keep Reish Lakish, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish and bar Lakisha as supported local identity candidates, and distinguish remembered questioning habits from present speech.
must_avoid: Do not treat the marriage offer at :12 alone as a completed wedding.
Do not place Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat in the earlier Jordan encounter or merge every scene into one meeting.
Do not turn disagreement about tool completion into a timeless opposition between the people.
unresolved_not_scored: The initial offer is conditional; do not extract a completed wedding from :12 alone. Her reference to widowhood in :15 supplies additional marital evidence.
The story’s Reish Lakish, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish and bar Lakisha are strong within-episode identity candidates. Wider historical matching is a separate step.

must_preserve: Keep Shmuel and Avlet as participants in the watching scene, and Avlet’s fatal-snakebite statement as a prediction about an unnamed worker.
Direct Shmuel’s מאי עבדת question to the returning worker, whose return is narrated, rather than to Avlet.
Keep the worker’s account of sparing a companion embarrassment separate from Shmuel’s later teaching that charity saves from death.
must_avoid: Do not report the predicted worker’s death as an event or assign the worker’s account to Avlet.
Do not infer Avlet’s biography or status as a sage from his name and presence alone.
unresolved_not_scored: The role of Avlet is not supplied by his name alone. Do not infer a sage classification or biography from this passage.

must_preserve: Keep Rabbi Akiva’s unnamed daughter as a person and preserve her child-of claim from דרבי עקיבא הויא ליה ברתא.
Keep the astrologers’ fatal wedding-day snakebite as a prediction, distinct from the narrated encounter with the snake.
Resolve אבוה in the next segment to Rabbi Akiva asking his daughter what she did, and retain her account of giving food to an unnamed poor man.
Keep Rabbi Akiva’s subsequent teaching that charity saves from death separate from his daughter’s reported action.
must_avoid: Do not omit the daughter because she lacks a dictionary name or invent a named groom.
Do not record the predicted death as fulfilled.
Do not settle who was worried by copying the translation over the masculine Hebrew הוה דאיג.
unresolved_not_scored: The groom is not named. Do not attach a named spouse from memory. The English translation’s worried subject differs from the masculine Hebrew הוה דאיג; no worried-person claim is accepted here.

must_preserve: Keep חנן הנחבא בר ברתיה דחוני המעגל as a two-step family path: Hanan is the child of an unnamed daughter of Honi HaMeaggel.
Keep the sages as senders and the schoolchildren as the visitors and speakers sent to Hanan.
Keep the children’s אבא, אבא as their form of address to Hanan and retain the request for rain.
must_avoid: Do not make Hanan Honi’s direct child or omit the unnamed mother.
Do not turn the children’s form of address into biological parenthood or place all the sending sages at the visit.
unresolved_not_scored: The mother’s personal name is not given. The children’s wording does not make them Hanan’s children.

must_preserve: Keep Rabbi Yosei bar Avin’s regular attendance before Rabbi Yosei of Yokrat, departure, and arrival before Rav Ashi in that order.
Read the conversation across the page break to resolve Rav Ashi’s recitation of a teaching attributed to Shmuel.
Keep אנא ניהו as the interlocutor’s local self-identification with Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Avin, while preserving the printed bar/ben name forms.
Link the later questions about leaving Rabbi Yosei of Yokrat to the earlier attendance story.
must_avoid: Do not put the former teacher, Rav Ashi and the quoted Shmuel into one meeting.
Do not treat regular attendance as a formal student appointment or lose the end of the earlier attendance relationship.
unresolved_not_scored: הוה שכיח קמיה states regular attendance, not a formal appointment as student. The printed bar Avin/ben Rabbi Avin difference remains visible even when this episode identifies the speaker.

must_preserve: Keep אביי קשישא as one complete name with its epithet, rather than two people.
Attribute the bridge-plank comparison in Sanhedrin 7a:6 to Abaye the Elder, separately from Rav Huna’s preceding comparison.
must_avoid: Do not merge this speaker into the familiar Abaye from the base name alone.
Do not create speech or a meeting between Abaye the Elder and Rav Huna merely from adjacent teachings.
unresolved_not_scored: Do not merge this speaker into the familiar Abaye solely because the base name matches. The passage does not settle that historical identity.
The preceding Rav Huna analogy is relevant context, but adjacency alone does not prove that either speaker addresses the other.

must_preserve: Keep רבי חייא רבא and רבי חייא רבה as the complete Hiyya name forms, with a supported spelling link within this passage.
Keep Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Shimon ben Halafta as participants in the dawn walk in the Arbel valley.
Direct Rabbi Hiyya’s speech to Rabbi Shimon ben Halafta and keep its biblical examples inside the spoken analogy.
must_avoid: Do not split רבא or רבה from Hiyya into the Babylonian Rava or Rabba.
Do not place Mordecai and Haman in the dawn walk or put the introductory reporter there without evidence.
unresolved_not_scored: The same paragraph has רבא then רבה. This supports a within-passage spelling link, not a link to the Babylonian Rava or Rabba.
The biblical narrative about Mordecai and Haman is quoted analogy, outside the walking scene.

must_preserve: Keep the sages asking Rabbi Abbahu about Rabbi Elai, and Rabbi Abbahu answering the sages.
Give the indirect phrase a person reading under אמרי לה אשה and a tractate reading under ואמרי לה מסכתא.
Keep the question-and-answer exchange shared while the type and meaning of the phrase change by reading.
must_avoid: Do not create an unconditional wife or marriage relation from wording also read as a tractate.
Do not put Rabbi Elai in the conversation or treat the translation’s second-marriage and Kodashim details as all explicit in the short Hebrew.
unresolved_not_scored: The translation explains a second marriage in the woman branch and a tractate of Kodashim in the study branch. Those details are explanations, not all explicit in the short Hebrew.
Rabbi Elai is being asked about; the passage does not put him in the conversation.

must_preserve: Keep רבין בר רב נחמן as a complete person name with an embedded Rav Nahman mention and a child-of claim.
Direct Rav Yehuda’s speech to Ravin bar Rav Nahman, preserving רבין אחי as the form of address.
Keep the stated custom for neighbors’ leaning trees as the content of Rav Yehuda’s speech.
must_avoid: Do not infer biological brotherhood between Rav Yehuda and Ravin from אחי alone.
Do not split Ravin’s name into unrelated speakers or transfer character offsets between differently abbreviated editions.
unresolved_not_scored: רבין אחי alone does not establish that Rav Yehuda and Ravin are biological brothers.
The saved abbreviated Rav Nahman mention and the expanded source edition should be linked by version-aware offsets, not assumed identical character positions.

must_preserve: Keep the unnamed female servant and her affiliation with Rabbi’s household, without requiring a personal name.
Keep the unnamed father and adult son, their family relationship, and the father’s striking of the son.
Record the servant’s declaration of a ban against the father and her stated reason using the stumbling-block prohibition.
must_avoid: Do not put Rabbi in the scene merely because his household is named or convert the household affiliation into kinship.
Do not replace the servant’s declaration with a settled claim about its institutional force without the surrounding evidence.
unresolved_not_scored: בית רבי is a household label. The passage does not name this woman or place Rabbi in the scene.
The text states that the servant declares a ban; its institutional force is discussed in the surrounding passage and should have its own evidence.
